graphNodes.name: Global Temperature
graphNodes.description: Observed global mean surface temperature remained near 1.43 C above the 1850-1900 average in 2025, with WMO synthesis and the NASA GISTEMP, NOAA NCEI, and Berkeley Earth records used here as the anchor. Satellite products such as AIRS are treated as supporting atmospheric context rather than replacements for the surface temperature record.

graphNodes.name: Methane Emissions
graphNodes.description: Atmospheric methane remains a high-leverage warming gas. NOAA reported a globally averaged marine-surface monthly mean of 1,940.46 ppb for February 2026, reflecting continued growth from agriculture, wetlands, waste, and fossil-system leaks.

graphNodes.name: Deforestation
graphNodes.description: Clearance of forest canopy. Tracked by Landsat and MODIS land-cover data products (available via NASA Earthdata LP DAAC), Global Forest Watch registers a net loss of 10 million hectares annually, leading to carbon sink degradation.

graphNodes.name: Industry Farming
graphNodes.description: Monoculture farming and intensive livestock rearing. MODIS vegetation indices (EVI/NDVI) and SMAP soil moisture data track associated land degradation. Fertilizers release ~150 Tg of nitrogen annually, exceeding biogeochemical flows.

graphNodes.name: Agricultural Demand
graphNodes.description: Global agricultural demand for food, particularly meat and dairy. MODIS and Landsat agricultural land-use mapping monitor this demand as it drives deforestation and cropland expansion.

graphNodes.name: Urbanization
graphNodes.description: The conversion of rural landscapes into dense urban settlements. VIIRS Nighttime Lights and MODIS land cover change products monitor this expansion, which drives infrastructure demand, localized warming, and migration.

graphNodes.name: Fast Fashion
graphNodes.description: Rapid production of low-cost clothing, leading to massive textile waste. Supply chain impacts are monitored via OCO-2 (industrial emissions) and Landsat (cotton irrigation water depletion) data products.

graphNodes.name: Migration
graphNodes.description: Displacement of populations driven by rising sea levels (monitored by Sentinel-6 and Jason altimetry) and severe drought indices derived from GRACE gravity mass changes.

graphNodes.name: Resource Depletion
graphNodes.description: Rapid depletion of fresh water aquifers and arable topsoil. GRACE and GRACE-FO gravity mass change data show critical groundwater aquifer depletion globally, crossing local freshwater boundaries.

graphNodes.name: Carbon Emission
graphNodes.description: This anchor uses atmospheric CO2 burden as the forcing proxy for carbon emissions. NOAA reported a Mauna Loa monthly average of 432.34 ppm for May 2026, capturing the cumulative warming pressure created by fossil combustion and land-use change.

graphNodes.name: Personal Conveyance
graphNodes.description: Reliance on private fossil-fueled vehicles. Associated urban NOx emissions are tracked by the TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution) satellite instrument.

graphNodes.name: Compound Climate Hazards
graphNodes.description: Co-occurring or sequential heat, heavy-rainfall, drought, wildfire, cyclone, and flood hazards. This is a bounded hazard-regime concept, not a catch-all for atmospheric anomalies.

graphNodes.name: El Niño
graphNodes.description: The warming phase of the ENSO pattern. Monitored via sea surface temperature anomalies from MODIS and sea surface height variations from Sentinel-6 and Jason satellites.

graphNodes.name: La Niña
graphNodes.description: The cooling phase of the ENSO pattern. It reorganizes tropical rainfall, sharpens drought-flood contrasts, and shifts storm tracks across the Pacific, the Americas, Africa, and Asia.

graphNodes.name: AMOC Slowdown
graphNodes.description: Weakening Atlantic overturning circulation can redistribute heat, alter European and tropical rainfall, and increase the risk of abrupt regional climate disruptions.

graphNodes.name: Wet-Bulb Heat
graphNodes.description: Combined heat and humidity extremes push human survivability limits, reduce labor capacity, and strain power, health, and cooling systems during prolonged heat events.

graphNodes.name: Monsoon Volatility
graphNodes.description: Erratic monsoon onset, breaks, and retreat intensify flood-drought swings, destabilizing food production, water storage, and hydro-dependent economies.

graphNodes.name: Permafrost Thaw
graphNodes.description: Frozen northern soils are thawing, releasing greenhouse gases, destabilizing roads and settlements, and amplifying Arctic carbon feedback loops.

graphNodes.name: Rain-on-Snow Flood Risk
graphNodes.description: Warming shifts cold-season storms toward rain falling onto existing snowpack, producing rapid runoff pulses, flood surges, and operational stress for mountain basins.

graphNodes.name: Peak Glacier Runoff Passage
graphNodes.description: Some glacier-fed basins are moving past the stage of rising meltwater supply and into long-term decline, changing the reliability of downstream seasonal water systems.

graphNodes.name: Marine Pathogen Range Expansion
graphNodes.description: Warmer water and changing coastal conditions expand the range or seasonality of marine pathogens that threaten shellfish safety, fisheries, and coastal health systems.

graphNodes.name: Thermal Stratification Intensification
graphNodes.description: Warming and freshening strengthen density layering in coastal and shelf waters, reducing vertical mixing, oxygen renewal, and resilience against low-oxygen events.

graphNodes.name: Delta Salt Intrusion Fronts
graphNodes.description: Salt fronts can push farther inland in deltas and estuaries as sea level rises, river discharge weakens, and storm-driven water levels press saline water into farms and intakes.

graphNodes.name: Oceanic Upwelling Disruptions
graphNodes.description: Changes in winds, circulation, and stratification can disrupt coastal and eastern-boundary upwelling, reducing nutrient delivery and destabilizing highly productive marine food systems.

graphNodes.name: Extreme Precipitation Intensity
graphNodes.description: A warmer atmosphere can dump more water in short bursts, increasing the intensity of rainfall events that overwhelm drainage, utilities, and river management systems.

graphNodes.name: Tropical Cyclone Rapid Intensification
graphNodes.description: Warmer ocean conditions and favorable atmospheric setups can increase the likelihood that tropical cyclones intensify quickly before landfall, compressing preparation time and raising surge risk.

graphNodes.name: Pyrocumulonimbus Smoke Injection
graphNodes.description: Extreme fires can generate pyrocumulonimbus storms that loft smoke into the upper atmosphere, altering transport pathways and extending the lifetime of fire-emitted aerosols.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Permafrost Erosion
graphNodes.description: Arctic coasts underlain by thawing permafrost can erode rapidly as warmer ground, sea-ice loss, and wave attack destabilize bluffs, roads, settlements, and shore infrastructure.

graphNodes.name: Baseline Water Stress
graphNodes.description: Persistent imbalance between water demand and available supply raises the baseline fragility of cities, farms, power systems, and river ecosystems.

graphNodes.name: Groundwater Depletion
graphNodes.description: Aquifers are being drawn down faster than they recharge, turning hidden water reserves into a long-lived constraint on farming, drinking water, and ecosystem resilience.

graphNodes.name: Heat-Related Mortality Burden
graphNodes.description: Extreme heat becomes a mortality burden when exposure, age, chronic illness, housing, and care-system access combine beyond safe recovery limits.

graphNodes.name: Air Pollution Health Burden
graphNodes.description: Ambient ozone, particulates, and combustion by-products translate transport and industrial activity into chronic respiratory, cardiovascular, and mortality risk.

graphNodes.name: Occupational Heat Exposure
graphNodes.description: Rising heat and humidity reduce safe work capacity, increase injury risk, and push labor-intensive sectors into direct climate-health loss.

graphNodes.name: Data Centers
graphNodes.description: Server campuses concentrate electricity demand, cooling water needs, backup generation, and land-use pressures in already stressed urban and industrial corridors.

graphNodes.name: AI Data Centers
graphNodes.description: Rapid buildout of compute-heavy AI facilities drives outsized electricity growth, cooling demand, semiconductor supply-chain impacts, and local grid congestion.

graphNodes.name: Semiconductor Fabs
graphNodes.description: Advanced chip fabrication ties compute growth to ultrapure water demand, process energy, fluorinated gases, and highly concentrated industrial supply chains.

graphNodes.name: Telecom Backbone
graphNodes.description: Long-haul fiber, switching nodes, and transmission corridors keep digital traffic moving between cities, regions, and countries while concentrating network fragility.

graphNodes.name: Mobile Towers / Wireless
graphNodes.description: Distributed towers, radio access equipment, and wireless backhaul extend the digital footprint across cities, highways, and rural corridors.

graphNodes.name: Internet Exchange Points
graphNodes.description: Carrier hotels and exchange points are compact but high-leverage hubs where networks physically interconnect and route large volumes of traffic.

graphNodes.name: Subsea Cables
graphNodes.description: Undersea cables and landing stations carry most international data traffic, making digital connectivity depend on a small number of coastal routes and repair pathways.

graphNodes.name: Food Waste
graphNodes.description: Loss and disposal across farms, retailers, kitchens, and landfills turn food systems into avoidable methane, water, and land-use pressure.

graphNodes.name: Aviation
graphNodes.description: Aircraft operations combine jet-fuel combustion, contrails, airport infrastructure, and high-altitude climate forcing in a fast-growing mobility system.

graphNodes.name: Shipping
graphNodes.description: Global shipping links freight demand to bunker fuel combustion, port congestion, marine pollution, and persistent trade-route emissions.

graphNodes.name: Cement / Concrete
graphNodes.description: Cement and concrete lock construction demand into kiln heat, calcination emissions, quarrying, and long-lived material throughput.

graphNodes.name: Steel
graphNodes.description: Steel production ties ore extraction, blast-furnace coal use, heat demand, and construction supply chains into a concentrated industrial footprint.

graphNodes.name: Plastics / Petrochemicals
graphNodes.description: Petrochemical production connects fossil feedstocks to plastics, solvents, fertilizers, and pervasive waste leakage across land and ocean systems.

graphNodes.name: Air Conditioning / Refrigerants
graphNodes.description: Cooling systems combine growing electricity demand with potent refrigerant leakage, making heat adaptation itself part of the climate story.

graphNodes.name: Fertilizer Production
graphNodes.description: Industrial fertilizer production ties fossil gas, ammonia synthesis, nitrous oxide risk, and runoff-intensive farming systems together.

graphNodes.name: Mining / Critical Minerals
graphNodes.description: Critical-mineral extraction expands pits, tailings, water draw, and energy use as battery, grid, and electronics demand accelerates.

graphNodes.name: Urban Sprawl / Housing
graphNodes.description: Low-density housing expansion turns land conversion, road building, construction materials, and household energy demand into long-lived urban pressure.

graphNodes.name: Clean Electricity
graphNodes.description: Low-emissions power is the backbone response that lets buildings, vehicles, and parts of industry cut fossil-fuel use without shifting emissions back to the grid.

graphNodes.name: Coal Power Retirement
graphNodes.description: Planned coal-plant retirement removes one of the most carbon-intensive power sources while avoiding abrupt closures that abandon workers and communities.

graphNodes.name: Renewable Energy Deployment
graphNodes.description: Scaling wind, solar, geothermal, and sustainable hydro displaces fossil generation when it is paired with grids, flexibility, and responsible siting.

graphNodes.name: Grid-Scale Energy Storage
graphNodes.description: Storage shifts electricity across hours and seasons, helping variable clean power meet demand and reducing reliance on high-emitting peaker plants.

graphNodes.name: Demand Response
graphNodes.description: Demand response pays or automates flexible electricity use so demand shifts away from stressed hours instead of requiring another fossil peaker plant.

graphNodes.name: Methane Leak Detection and Repair
graphNodes.description: Satellites, aircraft, ground sensors, and routine inspections can find large methane leaks quickly enough for operators and regulators to stop avoidable emissions.

graphNodes.name: Refrigerant Phase-Down
graphNodes.description: Replacing high-warming refrigerants, preventing leaks, and recovering gases at end of life cuts climate pollution while preserving access to cooling.

graphNodes.name: Carbon Dioxide Removal
graphNodes.description: Carbon dioxide removal can counter residual emissions, but it is a limited complement to rapid emissions cuts—not a substitute for delaying them.

graphNodes.name: Building Energy Efficiency
graphNodes.description: Better insulation, windows, lighting, controls, and appliances reduce the energy needed to keep buildings safe and comfortable.

graphNodes.name: Heat Pump Electrification
graphNodes.description: Heat pumps move heat rather than creating it through combustion, providing efficient heating and cooling as electricity gets cleaner.

graphNodes.name: Weatherization Retrofits
graphNodes.description: Air sealing, insulation, shading, and moisture control make existing homes cheaper to run and safer during heat, cold, smoke, and outages.

graphNodes.name: Passive Cooling Design
graphNodes.description: Shade, ventilation, reflective surfaces, thermal mass, trees, and building form can keep spaces cooler before mechanical air conditioning is needed.

graphNodes.name: Building Performance Standards
graphNodes.description: Measured building-performance standards require large buildings to improve actual energy or emissions outcomes over time instead of relying only on design intent.

graphNodes.name: Public Transit Expansion
graphNodes.description: Frequent, reliable transit reduces the need for private car trips while expanding access to work, school, health care, and essential services.

graphNodes.name: Walking and Cycling Networks
graphNodes.description: Safe walking, cycling, and wheelchair networks replace short car trips while improving health and access to daily needs.

graphNodes.name: Electric Vehicle Transition
graphNodes.description: Electric vehicles can cut oil use and urban tailpipe pollution, especially as grids get cleaner, but they do not solve congestion, road danger, or car-dependent land use.

graphNodes.name: Low-Carbon Cement and Concrete
graphNodes.description: Material efficiency, lower-clinker blends, alternative binders, clean heat, and carbon capture can reduce the process and fuel emissions built into concrete.

graphNodes.name: Near-Zero Emissions Steel
graphNodes.description: Material efficiency, scrap recycling, clean-electric furnaces, hydrogen-based reduction, and carbon capture can sharply reduce steel emissions.

graphNodes.name: Ecosystem Restoration
graphNodes.description: Restoring forests, wetlands, grasslands, rivers, reefs, and soils can rebuild carbon storage, biodiversity, water regulation, and local protection when the original drivers of loss are removed.

graphNodes.name: Multi-Hazard Early Warning
graphNodes.description: Forecasts save lives only when observations, communications, trusted messengers, evacuation options, and response plans deliver an understandable warning to everyone at risk.

graphNodes.name: Urban Heat Action Plans
graphNodes.description: Heat action plans combine forecasts, public-health triggers, worker protections, outreach, cooling sites, shade, and building measures before dangerous heat arrives.

graphNodes.name: Equitable Cooling Access
graphNodes.description: Safe cooling access combines efficient equipment, affordable electricity, weatherized housing, public cooling spaces, and outage protection for people most exposed to heat.

graphNodes.name: Flood-Resilient Infrastructure
graphNodes.description: Upgraded drainage, bridges, utilities, buildings, floodplains, and protective infrastructure reduce damage when rainfall, rivers, or seas exceed historical design conditions.

graphNodes.name: Water Reuse and Recycling
graphNodes.description: Treating and reusing wastewater for industry, irrigation, recharge, or potable supply can reduce pressure on rivers and aquifers when health and energy safeguards are strong.

graphNodes.name: Climate-Resilient Agriculture
graphNodes.description: Diversified crops, healthier soils, efficient water use, agroforestry, climate information, and risk protection help farms withstand heat, drought, flood, pests, and market shocks.

graphNodes.name: Planned Relocation
graphNodes.description: Planned relocation creates a rights-based path out of places that cannot be protected safely, while preserving housing, livelihoods, culture, services, and community choice.

graphNodes.name: Nature-Based Adaptation
graphNodes.description: Wetlands, mangroves, urban trees, healthy soils, dunes, reefs, and connected habitats can reduce flood, heat, erosion, and water risks while supporting biodiversity.

graphNodes.name: Aquifer Overdraft
graphNodes.description: Tracks chronic groundwater overdraft where withdrawals outpace recharge and long-lived water security declines.

graphNodes.name: River Flow Regime Change
graphNodes.description: Tracks changing flow timing and magnitude where warming, snowmelt change, and drought alter river-system reliability.

graphNodes.name: Reservoir Storage Instability
graphNodes.description: Reservoir Storage Instability is represented here through reservoir storage instability, measured in usable storage anomaly, refill reliability, or operating shortfall against a stated rule for named reservoir and contributing basin. Storage levels combine climate, operations, demands, transfers, and measurement choices.

graphNodes.name: Reservoir Operating Shortfall
graphNodes.description: Tracks the operating consequence when reservoirs cannot reliably deliver expected storage, release timing, or generation support.

graphNodes.name: Shift in Snowmelt Timing
graphNodes.description: Tracks observed shifts in when seasonal snow melts, making this a bounded timing signal rather than a generic cryosphere placeholder.

graphNodes.name: Soil Moisture Collapse
graphNodes.description: Active tracking of satellite-derived soil moisture anomalies; requires CDS/Earthdata logins for programmatic data access.

graphNodes.name: Flash Flood Regime
graphNodes.description: Tracks shifts in the frequency or intensity of short-duration flood-producing rainfall and runoff, rather than a vague generic flood alarm.

graphNodes.name: Drought Persistence
graphNodes.description: Monitors multi-season drought persistence and carryover effects in soil and reservoirs.

graphNodes.name: Freshwater Lens Thinning in Small Islands
graphNodes.description: Tracks thinning and salinization of small-island freshwater lenses, keeping this node tied to a real hydrogeology problem rather than a vague water-stress abstraction.

graphNodes.name: Drinking Water Treatment Stress
graphNodes.description: Links salinity, turbidity, and algal blooms to increased water utility treatment complexity and costs.

graphNodes.name: Watershed Forest Loss
graphNodes.description: Tracks loss of forest cover and buffering function in critical watersheds, where land-cover change reshapes runoff, erosion, habitat quality, and downstream water reliability.

graphNodes.name: Wastewater Infrastructure Overflow
graphNodes.description: Tracks wastewater overflow risk where stormwater, inundation, or plant-capacity limits cause collection and treatment systems to exceed safe handling thresholds.

graphNodes.name: Wastewater Bypass Discharge
graphNodes.description: Tracks bypass or overflow discharge events where utilities release untreated or partially treated wastewater under hydraulic stress.

graphNodes.name: Irrigation Water Inefficiency
graphNodes.description: Tracks irrigation losses and weak delivery efficiency where scarce basin water is spent without proportional crop benefit.

graphNodes.name: Hydropower Reliability Decline
graphNodes.description: Tracks falling hydropower reliability where drought, altered runoff timing, and reservoir stress reduce dependable generation.

graphNodes.name: Basin Treaty Breakdown
graphNodes.description: Monitors transboundary basin cooperation, allocation treaties, and drought-era sharing strains.

graphNodes.name: Desalination Dependence
graphNodes.description: Tracks growing desalination reliance, energy footprint, and marine brine disposal tradeoffs.

graphNodes.name: Ice Sheet Mass Loss
graphNodes.description: Compiles satellite observations of Greenland and Antarctic ice sheet mass loss.

graphNodes.name: Glacial Lake Outburst Flood Risk
graphNodes.description: Tracks glacial lake outburst-flood risk where retreating ice and unstable moraine or ice dams increase downstream hazard exposure.

graphNodes.name: Sea Ice Season Loss
graphNodes.description: Tracks sea ice extent anomalies and Arctic feedback loops.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Inundation Risk
graphNodes.description: Tracks recurring and escalating coastal flood exposure from sea-level rise, shoreline erosion, and higher baseline water levels rather than a generic coastal alarm node.

graphNodes.name: Thermokarst Expansion
graphNodes.description: Tracks expanding thermokarst terrain where thawing ice-rich permafrost causes subsidence, ponding, and infrastructure instability.

graphNodes.name: Arctic Shipping Expansion
graphNodes.description: Tracks observed expansion of Arctic shipping activity as navigable sea-ice windows lengthen, while keeping the node grounded in route and traffic evidence rather than a generic northern trade thesis.

graphNodes.name: Polar Infrastructure Failure
graphNodes.description: Tracks failure risk in polar and subarctic infrastructure where thawing ground undermines foundations, pipelines, roads, and remote facilities.

graphNodes.name: Snow Drought
graphNodes.description: Tracks snow-drought conditions where snowpack is unusually low for the season, without implying every snow deficit maps to glacier dependence.

graphNodes.name: Loss of Firn Meltwater Storage Capacity
graphNodes.description: Tracks loss of firn meltwater storage capacity on land ice, a narrower and more defensible framing than treating firn depletion as a free-floating glacier tail.

graphNodes.name: Glacier-Fed Water Dependence
graphNodes.description: Tracks places whose seasonal water systems rely on glacier runoff, making dependence itself the defensible exposure signal rather than any one downstream impact.

graphNodes.name: Oceanic Deoxygenation
graphNodes.description: Oceanic deoxygenation is distinct from coastal hypoxia because it describes the measured decline of dissolved oxygen across the open ocean and abyssal waters, documented globally in the primary Science synthesis on oxygen loss in open-ocean and coastal systems.

graphNodes.name: Antarctic Bottom Water Decline
graphNodes.description: Antarctic Bottom Water decline is treated as a separate deep-ocean anchor because primary observations show reduced abyssal overturning and ventilation in the Australian Antarctic Basin, thinning oxygenated bottom layers and weakening deep ocean renewal.

graphNodes.name: Ocean Acidification
graphNodes.description: Ocean acidification is promoted to anchor status because NOAA PMEL documents multi-decadal observations showing CO2 uptake is measurably changing seawater chemistry, pH, and carbonate conditions across the global ocean.

graphNodes.name: Pacific Decadal Oscillation
graphNodes.description: Pacific Decadal Oscillation is retained as a canonical basin-scale climate mode because NOAA PSL maintains a long-running monthly PDO index time series, supporting direct empirical monitoring rather than inferential labeling.

graphNodes.name: Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation
graphNodes.description: Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation is kept as a monitored North Atlantic variability signal because NOAA PSL publishes a long monthly AMO index record, making it a cleaner anchor than a vague Atlantic regime placeholder.

graphNodes.name: Atlantic Niño/Niña
graphNodes.description: Atlantic Nino/Nina is modelled as a distinct tropical Atlantic SST variability mode because the Nature Climate Change study identifies it as a canonical variability phenomenon with climate teleconnections separate from ENSO and the Indian Ocean Dipole.

graphNodes.name: Indian Ocean Dipole
graphNodes.description: Indian Ocean Dipole is promoted to anchor status because NOAA CPC updates the Dipole Mode Index monthly and explicitly tracks positive and negative IOD phases as an observed climate phenomenon.

graphNodes.name: Marine Fisheries Collapse
graphNodes.description: Tracks stock depletion trends and climate-driven marine protein insecurity.

graphNodes.name: Fish Landing Supply Disruption
graphNodes.description: Tracks instability in fish landings and local seafood supply as a practical consequence of shifting stocks, access, and disrupted coastal operations.

graphNodes.name: Ocean Circulation Regime Shifts
graphNodes.description: Tracks ocean circulation regime shifts as a broad parent-level circulation node, without collapsing it into any single AMOC-collapse claim.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Hypoxia
graphNodes.description: Monitors oxygen depletion in coastal waters driven by warming, stratification, and runoff.

graphNodes.name: Marine Food-Web Reorganization
graphNodes.description: Tracks marine food-web reorganization under changing ocean structure and species movement, avoiding a misleading implication of uniform collapse everywhere.

graphNodes.name: Ocean Salinity Stratification
graphNodes.description: Tracks changing salinity layering and vertical structure in the ocean, a directly observed physical pattern with strong defensibility.

graphNodes.name: Harmful Algal Blooms
graphNodes.description: Tracks toxic or otherwise damaging algal bloom outbreaks across fresh, estuarine, and coastal waters where warming and nutrient stress can translate into ecological and public-health harm.

graphNodes.name: Pelagic Species Redistribution
graphNodes.description: Tracks redistribution of pelagic species across monitored occurrence and survey systems as habitat conditions and circulation patterns shift.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Storm-Surge Exposure
graphNodes.description: Tracks coastal storm-surge exposure using mapped flood-exposure context, making this a bounded coastal-hazard node rather than a vague littoral stress signal.

graphNodes.name: Land Carbon Sink Weakening
graphNodes.description: This anchor is inferred from the Global Carbon Budget 2025 FAQ reporting that climate change and variability are weakening natural land and ocean sinks, with the land sink substantially smaller than it would be without climate change over the recent decade.

graphNodes.name: Peat Oxidation Pulse
graphNodes.description: Peat oxidation is treated as a carbon-cycle feedback because NASA Earthdata maintains peatland data access and monitoring pathways relevant to peat carbon storage, drainage, fire, and release risk.

graphNodes.name: Tidal Wetland Carbon Reversal
graphNodes.description: Tidal wetland carbon reversal is modelled as a distinct coastal carbon feedback using NOAA blue-carbon program material on carbon storage in salt marsh, mangrove, and seagrass systems and the risk of reversal under disturbance and loss.

graphNodes.name: Ocean Carbon Uptake Weakening
graphNodes.description: This anchor is inferred from the Global Carbon Budget 2025 FAQ reporting that climate change has already weakened the ocean carbon sink relative to a no-climate-change baseline, reducing the climate-buffering role of ocean uptake.

graphNodes.name: Nocturnal Heat Stress
graphNodes.description: Nocturnal heat stress is treated as distinct from generic wet-bulb or daytime heat because the Nature Climate Change analysis isolates nighttime heat exposure as a separate human-recovery and survivability hazard.

graphNodes.name: Compound Day-Night Heat Extremes
graphNodes.description: Compound day-night heat extremes are modelled as a separate compound hazard because the same Nature Climate Change study distinguishes persistent 24-hour heat exposure from isolated daytime or nighttime heat stress.

graphNodes.name: Hail Hazard Shift
graphNodes.description: Hail hazard shift is included as a distinct severe-convective climate signal because the Nature Climate Change study links warming to a redistribution of hail-prone environments and associated crop risk.

graphNodes.name: Madden-Julian Oscillation
graphNodes.description: The Madden-Julian Oscillation is kept as a canonical intraseasonal tropical variability mode because NOAA CPC operationally tracks its wind, OLR, and forecast diagnostics and it materially modulates global rainfall and temperature anomaly pathways.

graphNodes.name: North Atlantic Oscillation
graphNodes.description: The North Atlantic Oscillation is retained as a canonical teleconnection because NOAA CPC maintains standardized daily and monthly index products dating back to 1950, making it an empirically monitored circulation mode rather than a speculative regional label.

graphNodes.name: Arctic Oscillation
graphNodes.description: The Arctic Oscillation is modelled separately from generic jet variability because NOAA CPC provides a standardized AO index tied to polar-cap height anomalies and cold-season circulation structure.

graphNodes.name: Pacific-North American Pattern
graphNodes.description: The Pacific-North American pattern is included as a distinct teleconnection because NOAA CPC tracks it as a standardized monthly-varying circulation mode with direct North American weather relevance.

graphNodes.name: Southern Annular Mode
graphNodes.description: Southern Annular Mode is sourced from NOAA CPC Antarctic Oscillation monitoring and treated as the canonical Southern Hemisphere annular circulation mode rather than duplicating AAO and SAM as separate nodes.

graphNodes.name: Quasi-Biennial Oscillation
graphNodes.description: The Quasi-Biennial Oscillation is included because NASA maintains near-real-time and historical QBO observations from radiosondes, reanalysis, and satellite data, supporting its role as a measured stratospheric variability mode.

graphNodes.name: Persistent Atmospheric Blocking
graphNodes.description: Tracks long-lived atmospheric blocking patterns that hold weather in place and can prolong heat, drought, rainfall, or smoke episodes over the same region.

graphNodes.name: Atmospheric Moisture Amplification
graphNodes.description: Tracks amplification of atmospheric moisture and heat-humidity stress where warming lifts water-vapor load and pushes conditions toward more dangerous apparent heat.

graphNodes.name: Lightning Ignition under Fire Weather Conditions
graphNodes.description: Tracks fire-prone weather patterns where dryness, instability, and lightning align to raise wildfire ignition and spread risk.

graphNodes.name: Atmospheric Evaporative Demand
graphNodes.description: Tracks dry atmospheric demand and moisture stress where warmer air and circulation shifts intensify evaporation and vegetation desiccation.

graphNodes.name: Black Carbon Darkening of Snow
graphNodes.description: Tracks dark particle deposition on snow and ice where reduced surface reflectivity can accelerate melt and amplify polar heat absorption.

graphNodes.name: Climate Penalty on Surface Ozone
graphNodes.description: Tracks the precursor and weather conditions that raise the likelihood of harmful ground-level ozone formation.

graphNodes.name: Persistent Rossby Wave Patterns
graphNodes.description: Tracks stalled or slow-moving planetary-wave patterns that can lock in anomalous heat, storm, or drought conditions.

graphNodes.name: Smoke Exposure Burden
graphNodes.description: Tracks the health and air-quality burden of repeated smoke exposure from wildfire and landscape fire events.

graphNodes.name: Marine Low-Cloud Decline
graphNodes.description: Tracks retreat or thinning of reflective low cloud decks where cloud-cover change can alter regional radiation balance and surface heating.

graphNodes.name: Aerosol Cooling Loss
graphNodes.description: Scientific assessment of aerosol cooling loss, radiative forcing masking, and climate budget feedbacks.

graphNodes.name: Grid Peak Load Stress
graphNodes.description: Links extreme heat waves and AI data center energy growth to peak load grid reliability stress.

graphNodes.name: Peaker Plant Lock-In
graphNodes.description: Tracks the persistence of fossil peaker capacity where reliability markets and peak-load planning still favor fast-start gas generation.

graphNodes.name: Transmission Buildout Lag
graphNodes.description: Tracks regional power grid constraints, interconnection queues, and permitting delays.

graphNodes.name: Transformer Supply Bottleneck
graphNodes.description: Tracks grid-equipment bottlenecks where transformer and substation constraints slow interconnection, reliability upgrades, and broader grid expansion.

graphNodes.name: Gas Power Dependence
graphNodes.description: Tracks dependence on gas-fired power as a continuing electricity-system anchor that shapes emissions, reliability choices, and fossil fallback.

graphNodes.name: Industrial Heat Decarbonization Gap
graphNodes.description: Tracks the decarbonization bottleneck in industrial process heat, where reliable high-temperature demand still outpaces electrification and low-emissions alternatives.

graphNodes.name: Cement Process Emissions
graphNodes.description: Tracks the irreducible process-emissions burden of cement production, especially clinker calcination, inside the wider construction materials system.

graphNodes.name: Steel Decarbonization Gap
graphNodes.description: Tracks the gap between current steelmaking routes and the lower-emissions technologies, scrap systems, and clean-power inputs needed for a credible transition.

graphNodes.name: Critical Mineral Extraction Pressure
graphNodes.description: Tracks the environmental and supply pressure created by rising demand for transition minerals across batteries, grids, and electrified industry.

graphNodes.name: Battery Supply Chain Pressure
graphNodes.description: Tracks strain across battery manufacturing and upstream materials systems as electrification scales faster than resilient low-impact supply can follow.

graphNodes.name: Semiconductor Fabrication Footprint
graphNodes.description: Details water and electricity footprint metrics of advanced silicon fabrication facilities.

graphNodes.name: Cooling Water Competition
graphNodes.description: Reflects data center and power plant cooling water demands competing with municipal and agricultural basins.

graphNodes.name: Backup Generator Dependence
graphNodes.description: Tracks infrastructure dependence on diesel or gas backup generation where primary grid resilience remains insufficient for critical operations.

graphNodes.name: Energy Affordability Crisis
graphNodes.description: Tracks the household affordability side of climate-energy stress where high bills, peak demand, and volatile supply turn energy access into a resilience problem.

graphNodes.name: Utility Disconnection Risk
graphNodes.description: Tracks shutoff and service-loss risk where energy burden crosses into direct household exposure during extreme conditions.

graphNodes.name: Renewable Curtailment Losses
graphNodes.description: Tracks renewable generation that cannot fully reach load because wires, interconnection, storage, or operating flexibility lag behind deployment.

graphNodes.name: Aviation Demand Growth
graphNodes.description: Tracks rising aviation activity as a direct transport-emissions and high-altitude forcing pressure, instead of leaving it as a generic modeled demand tail.

graphNodes.name: Shipping Lane Disruption
graphNodes.description: Details shipping lane disruptions and transit delays in key canals (Panama, Suez) due to climate extremes and geopolitics.

graphNodes.name: Freight Electrification Gap
graphNodes.description: Tracks the gap between current freight fleets and a credible heavy-duty electrification transition using truck-specific market and policy evidence.

graphNodes.name: Port Heat-Related Operational Vulnerability
graphNodes.description: Tracks heat-related operational vulnerability at ports, intentionally softer than a broad port-climate hazard claim and not a proxy for surge or flood exposure.

graphNodes.name: Road Freight Diesel Lock-In
graphNodes.description: Tracks diesel lock-in, commercial truck emissions, and electric heavy-duty vehicle transition barriers.

graphNodes.name: Airport Climate Exposure
graphNodes.description: Tracks airport exposure to climate stress using official airport registries and resilience guidance, especially around heat, flooding, and operational constraints.

graphNodes.name: Airport Operational Disruption
graphNodes.description: Tracks airport service disruption as the operational layer between climate exposure and wider transport or economic consequences.

graphNodes.name: Bridge Scour Exposure
graphNodes.description: Tracks bridge scour exposure through official bridge inventory and hydraulic-risk practice, making it one of the stronger infrastructure-tail nodes.

graphNodes.name: Rail Heat Buckling
graphNodes.description: Tracks heat-driven rail deformation and service risk where hotter track conditions can force slow orders, cancellations, and higher derailment exposure.

graphNodes.name: Biodiversity Intactness Loss
graphNodes.description: Tracks loss of ecosystem intactness where habitat degradation and fragmentation remove species richness and functional resilience.

graphNodes.name: Wildfire Regime Shift
graphNodes.description: Monitors changes in fire weather, active thermal anomalies, burn severity, and smoke burden; requires a free API map key.

graphNodes.name: Forest Fragmentation
graphNodes.description: Links forest canopy edge effects and spatial fragmentation to biodiversity loss.

graphNodes.name: Mangrove Buffer Loss
graphNodes.description: Maps mangrove extent decline and models coastal storm protection and wave attenuation benefits.

graphNodes.name: Reef Structural Collapse
graphNodes.description: Monitors thermal bleaching heat stress and framework calcification loss.

graphNodes.name: Pollinator Service Decline
graphNodes.description: Details wild and managed pollinator declines and risks to global crop yields.

graphNodes.name: Freshwater Ecosystem Collapse
graphNodes.description: Tracks degradation and loss of river, lake, and wetland habitats (SDG 6.6.1).

graphNodes.name: Species Range Contraction
graphNodes.description: Tracks species range contraction through occurrence and assessment frameworks, without implying that every contraction is climate-driven by default.

graphNodes.name: Insect Biomass Decline
graphNodes.description: Tracks broad declines in insect abundance and biomass where habitat simplification, warming, and pollinator stress start to erode food-web and crop-support functions.

graphNodes.name: Soil Humus Decline
graphNodes.description: Tracks declining soil humus and organic carbon as a foundational soil-fertility and water-retention loss, rather than a free-floating agricultural residue node.

graphNodes.name: Urban Tree Canopy Loss
graphNodes.description: Tracks decline in urban tree canopy where heat, drought, pests, and development reduce shade, cooling, and stormwater-buffering function.

graphNodes.name: Crop Yield Volatility
graphNodes.description: Ties climate variance to global yield volatility in major staple crops (wheat, rice, maize).

graphNodes.name: Farm Heat Stress
graphNodes.description: Quantifies agricultural labor-hour losses and occupational exposures under rising wet-bulb heat.

graphNodes.name: Livestock Disease Pressure
graphNodes.description: Tracks animal-health pressure where warming, vectors, and intensified production increase livestock disease exposure.

graphNodes.name: Fertilizer Price Shock
graphNodes.description: Tracks fertilizer affordability stress where energy prices, trade disruption, and nutrient dependence spill directly into farming costs.

graphNodes.name: Feed Crop Dependency
graphNodes.description: Tracks livestock dependence on feed-crop systems that amplify land, fertilizer, and water pressure across food production.

graphNodes.name: Food Import Exposure
graphNodes.description: Tracks dependence on imported food, trade bottlenecks, and price-sensitive supply shocks rather than acting as a catch-all proxy for food insecurity.

graphNodes.name: Cold Chain Failure Risk
graphNodes.description: Details cold chain storage and logistics vulnerabilities under extreme heat events.

graphNodes.name: Fishery Protein Dependence
graphNodes.description: Tracks populations and food systems that rely heavily on fish as a protein source, making fisheries disruption a direct food-security exposure rather than a vague social spillover.

graphNodes.name: Agricultural Labor Exposure
graphNodes.description: Tracks agricultural work exposure where heat stress and unsafe field conditions reduce labor capacity and harvest reliability.

graphNodes.name: Topsoil Erosion Acceleration
graphNodes.description: Tracks faster topsoil loss where exposed fields, runoff, and degraded land management weaken long-term agricultural productivity.

graphNodes.name: Insurance Retreat
graphNodes.description: Documents insurance premium increases, carrier withdrawals, and nonrenewals in climate-exposed housing markets.

graphNodes.name: Mortgage Market Exposure
graphNodes.description: Links climate hazard risks to mortgage lending standards, securitization, and systemic financial exposure.

graphNodes.name: Public Health Heat Burden
graphNodes.description: Tracks heat-related illness, mortality, and clinical-system strain, keeping the node anchored to health outcomes and care-system stress rather than broad social distress.

graphNodes.name: Vector-Borne Disease Expansion
graphNodes.description: Tracks bounded climate-linked expansion of malaria, dengue, and other vector-sensitive disease exposure zones.

graphNodes.name: Adaptation Capital Shortfall
graphNodes.description: Tracks adaptation capital shortfalls, funding deficits, and international public finance flows.

graphNodes.name: Critical Infrastructure Fragility
graphNodes.description: Ties climate hazard exposure to concrete service failures in transport, utility, and power networks, and should be read as an operational systems node rather than a generic downstream bucket.

graphNodes.name: Disaster Recovery Inequality
graphNodes.description: Tracks uneven recovery capacity, aid access, and funding distribution after climate shocks, making it a bounded recovery-governance node rather than a generic injustice bucket.

graphNodes.name: Relocation Governance Capacity
graphNodes.description: Tracks whether institutions can plan, finance, legalize, and service relocation or managed retreat, rather than implying any broad political capacity claim.

graphNodes.name: Climate Litigation Pressure
graphNodes.description: Tracks rising climate-litigation pressure where liability, disclosure, adaptation, and rights claims increasingly shape public and private climate decision-making.

graphNodes.name: Conflict Risk Escalation
graphNodes.description: Analyzes climate-induced disasters acting as conflict risk multipliers through displacement and food systems.

graphNodes.name: Talik Expansion
graphNodes.description: Talik Expansion is represented here through talik extent change, measured in unfrozen-zone thickness, area, or duration by method for named permafrost profile, lake setting, or infrastructure corridor. Taliks can be transient and refreeze.

graphNodes.name: Pollinator Colony Collapse
graphNodes.description: Pollinator Colony Collapse is represented here through pollinator population or colony loss, measured in standardized occupancy, abundance, colony survival, or loss rate for named pollinator population, colony system, or monitored landscape. Observed decline can reflect detection, management, or migration changes.

graphNodes.name: Nitrogen Fertilizer Runoff
graphNodes.description: Tracks excess nitrogen movement into waterways where fertilizer use degrades water quality and downstream ecosystem health.

graphNodes.name: Tropospheric Ozone
graphNodes.description: Tropospheric Ozone is represented here through ground-level ozone concentration and exposure, measured in parts per billion using stated averaging time, instrument, quality status, and exposure window for named regulatory monitor, airshed, urban area, agricultural region, or gridded model domain. Monitor siting, vertical mixing, transport, clouds, temperature, precursor chemistry, missing hours, and model resolution affect exposure estimates.

graphNodes.name: Marine Heatwaves
graphNodes.description: Marine Heatwaves is represented here through marine heatwave duration, intensity, and affected-ocean area above a seasonally varying threshold, measured in event-days, degree-Celsius-days, and percent ocean area reported separately for ocean grid cell, exclusive economic zone, marine ecoregion, basin, or declared global-ocean aggregation. Satellite retrieval, clouds and ice, coastal pixels, baseline length, product changes, subsurface heat, and spatial aggregation affect event metrics.

graphNodes.name: Fracking Wastewater Lakes
graphNodes.description: Fracking Wastewater Lakes is represented here through fracking wastewater containment risk, measured in reported volume, incident count, concentration, or compliance status for named hydraulic-fracturing operation or receiving water. Reporting and exposure pathways vary by site.

graphNodes.name: Cattle Grazing Overcompaction
graphNodes.description: Cattle Grazing Overcompaction is represented here through grazing-related soil compaction, measured in bulk density, penetration resistance, or infiltration change against local control for named paddock or pasture. Natural soil variation and seasonal moisture affect metrics.

graphNodes.name: Nitrous Oxide
graphNodes.description: Nitrous Oxide is represented here through anthropogenic nitrous-oxide emissions by source sector, measured in million tonnes N2O per year for global, country, source sector, or inventory jurisdiction. Activity data, fertilizer and manure inputs, emission factors, soil and climate heterogeneity, industrial-process allocation, country reporting, category coverage, and inventory revisions affect totals; EDGAR source rows do not provide numeric observation-level intervals.

graphNodes.name: Phytoplankton Decline
graphNodes.description: Tracks lower-ocean food-web stress where warming, acidification, and circulation change reduce plankton productivity.

graphNodes.name: Antarctic Shelf Instability
graphNodes.description: Antarctic Shelf Instability is represented here through antarctic ice-shelf basal melt, grounding-line position, and ice discharge, measured in meters per year, kilometers, and gigatonnes per year for named Antarctic ice-shelf and drainage basin. Ocean-cavity observations are sparse and instability thresholds have deep uncertainty; mass loss does not uniquely identify the mechanism.

graphNodes.name: Wildlife Habitat Patches
graphNodes.description: Studies spatial patterns in wildlife habitat patch sizes, connectivity, and trophic dynamics.

graphNodes.name: Topsoil Salinization Fields
graphNodes.description: Topsoil Salinization Fields is represented here through root-zone electrical conductivity and mapped salt-affected agricultural area, measured in decisiemens per meter, hectares, percent of land, and annual crop-loss cost reported separately for mapped agricultural field, irrigation district, country, or global assessment boundary. Salinity is spatially variable; sensor calibration, soil texture, soil moisture, naturally saline parent material, mapping method and older annual burden estimates affect interpretation.

graphNodes.name: Staple Food Price Volatility
graphNodes.description: Staple Food Price Volatility is represented here through staple-food price variance and affordability relative to household income, measured in local currency per kilogram, percent change, and percent of household expenditure for country, market, or subnational price series. Prices reflect currency changes, market selection, subsidies, reporting gaps, and quality differences as well as physical supply.

graphNodes.name: Sulfur Dioxide
graphNodes.description: Sulfur Dioxide is represented here through sulfur dioxide emission or ambient concentration, measured in tonnes per reporting period or parts per billion for named source, inventory, or monitor. Ambient concentration integrates transport, chemistry, deposition, and multiple sources.

graphNodes.name: Coral Bleaching
graphNodes.description: Coral Bleaching is represented here through coral bleaching severity and thermal stress, measured in percent coral colonies bleached, bleaching alert level, or degree-heating-weeks for named reef, ecoregion, or satellite grid cell. Satellite heat-stress products require field validation; susceptibility differs by species, acclimation, depth, and local stressors.

graphNodes.name: Invasive Species Encroachment
graphNodes.description: Invasive Species Encroachment is represented here through non-native occurrence range expansion, measured in new occupied grid cells per period for bounded region. Sensitive to taxonomic revisions, reporting effort, and uneven surveillance.

graphNodes.name: Deepwater Petroleum Operations
graphNodes.description: Deepwater Petroleum Operations is represented here through deepwater petroleum-spill risk signal, measured in documented risk assessment, incident, or loss-of-containment status for named offshore facility, well, or lease area. Risk analysis is probabilistic and not a spill prediction.

graphNodes.name: Volatile Organic Compounds
graphNodes.description: Volatile Organic Compounds is represented here through ambient volatile-organic-compound concentration and reactivity, measured in parts per billion by compound with sampling duration, method, and photochemical reactivity for named monitor, facility boundary, community, or airshed. Species volatility, sampling losses, detection limits, spatial gradients, and rapidly changing chemistry affect measurements.

graphNodes.name: Sea-Level Rise
graphNodes.description: Sea Level Rise is represented here through mean sea-level change relative to a declared baseline, measured in millimetres and millimetres per year for named station, transect, depth layer, ocean region, or quality-controlled analysis grid. Sparse sampling, platform changes, mapping, depth selection, seasonal aliasing, and model-data blending affect the estimate.

graphNodes.name: Tundra Methane Outgassing
graphNodes.description: Tundra Methane Outgassing is represented here through methane surface flux from tundra and permafrost landscapes, measured in milligrams CH4 per square metre per day for declared monitoring site, airshed, waterbody, facility, region, or emissions inventory boundary. Instrument calibration, source apportionment, inventory factors, sampling coverage, chemical transformation, and model resolution affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Soil Microbial Depletion
graphNodes.description: Soil Microbial Depletion is represented here through soil microbial biomass or activity, measured in microbial biomass, respiration, enzyme activity, or validated diversity index by method for named field, soil profile, and management unit. Methods capture different microbial properties and vary seasonally.

graphNodes.name: Surface Water Storage Instability
graphNodes.description: Surface Water Storage Instability is represented here through surface-water storage instability, measured in water-level, area, volume, affected-basin count, or water-balance anomaly against stated reference for global basin assessment or named surface-water body with aggregation retained. Natural seasonal variability, satellite detection, basin delineation and data gaps constrain inference.

graphNodes.name: Persistent Pesticide Residues in Sediment and Biota
graphNodes.description: Persistent Pesticide Residues in Sediment and Biota is represented here through persistent pesticide residue in sediment and biota, measured in micrograms per kilogram dry or wet weight by compound and matrix, with lipid-normalized concentration, biota-sediment accumulation factor, or trophic magnification factor reported separately for named water body, sediment reach, species, tissue, food-web sample, watershed, and reference site. Uptake differs by compound, species, tissue, diet, metabolism, lipid content, trophic position, sediment exposure, season, and legacy contamination; bioaccumulation and biomagnification are not interchangeable.

graphNodes.name: PM2.5 Particulates
graphNodes.description: Tracks fine particulate exposure at the PM2.5 scale as a widely used public-health and air-pollution indicator.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Hypoxic Dead Zones
graphNodes.description: Coastal Hypoxic Dead Zones is represented here through coastal dissolved oxygen, measured in site-specific concentration, biomass, oxygen demand, density gradient, or dissolved oxygen value for named estuary, coastal shelf, or marine basin. Hypoxia has natural and site-specific drivers; measurements must retain depth and timing.

graphNodes.name: Ice Albedo Feedback Loops
graphNodes.description: Ice Albedo Feedback Loops is represented here through sea-ice and snow albedo anomaly with absorbed shortwave radiation, measured in dimensionless albedo and watts per square meter for bounded Arctic sea-ice or snow-covered region. Cloud cover, melt ponds, snow grain size, aerosols, and surface type alter albedo and feedback strength.

graphNodes.name: Forest Dieback Areas
graphNodes.description: Forest Dieback Areas is represented here through forest dieback area and mortality, measured in area with verified canopy mortality or tree mortality rate against local baseline for named forest stand, landscape, or host population. Remote canopy change may reflect harvest, fire, or phenology.

graphNodes.name: Combined Sewer Overflow
graphNodes.description: Combined Sewer Overflow is represented here through combined sewer overflow event and volume, measured in overflow events, duration, and volume per reporting period for named CSO outfall, sewer shed, municipality, or reporting jurisdiction. Event volume and duration may be estimated; monitoring coverage and rainfall attribution vary.

graphNodes.name: Humanitarian Response Capacity Gap
graphNodes.description: Humanitarian Resource Gaps is represented here through oCHA FTS reported response-plan resource gap, measured in current USD shortfall and percent of current requirement for named released OCHA Humanitarian Programme Cycle plan and its declared locations. This is a reported financial resource gap, not a complete inventory of staff, supplies, access, logistics, local capacity, or delivered assistance. Reporting lag, unlinked flows, plan revisions, exchange rates, and off-FTS resources affect the estimate.

graphNodes.name: Carbon Monoxide
graphNodes.description: Carbon Monoxide is represented here through carbon-monoxide emission or concentration, measured in tonnes CO per reporting period or parts per million for named inventory source, monitor, or indoor setting. Concentration integrates transport, ventilation, and multiple sources.

graphNodes.name: Gulf Stream Transport and Position
graphNodes.description: Gulf Stream Transport and Position is represented here through gulf Stream section transport and path position, measured in Sverdrups of volume transport, kilometres or degrees latitude of a declared path contour, metres per second of velocity, and centimetres of cross-current dynamic sea-level difference reported separately for named current segment and cross-stream section such as the Florida Straits at 27 degrees north, Cape Hatteras separation region, or downstream longitude band with depth and contour definitions. Transport increases downstream through entrainment, path and volume transport are different, vertical layers can vary incoherently, cable and satellite records require corrections, and wind-driven gyre flow is not interchangeable with overturning.

graphNodes.name: Rapid Runoff Response
graphNodes.description: Hydrological Runoff Surges is represented here through peak runoff response relative to antecedent baseline flow, measured in unitless ratio and cubic metres per second for declared basin, aquifer, utility, catchment, floodplain, or administrative reporting area. Gauge and well coverage, withdrawals, return flows, groundwater-surface-water exchange, infrastructure reporting, model resolution, and revisions affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Population and Asset Exposure in Floodplains
graphNodes.description: Floodplain Exposure is represented here through population and assets within a declared flood-probability zone, measured in people, asset value, and percent of jurisdiction for declared basin, aquifer, utility, catchment, floodplain, or administrative reporting area. Gauge and well coverage, withdrawals, return flows, groundwater-surface-water exchange, infrastructure reporting, model resolution, and revisions affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Groundwater Depletion Wells
graphNodes.description: Tracks well-level groundwater drawdown where extraction exceeds recharge and drought resilience erodes.

graphNodes.name: Greenhouse Gas Effective Radiative Forcing
graphNodes.description: Greenhouse Gas Effective Radiative Forcing is represented here through long-lived greenhouse-gas effective radiative forcing, measured in watts per square metre relative to a stated preindustrial baseline, with gas contributions and uncertainty retained for global atmosphere, with the observing network and forcing calculation stated. Sparse sampling for some gases, calibration scale, atmospheric lifetime, spectral overlap, radiative efficiency, and rapid adjustments affect component and total estimates.

graphNodes.name: Ocean Heat Content
graphNodes.description: Heat stored in the upper ocean, interpreted at the geography and depth required by each relationship. ENSO dossiers use equatorial Pacific warm-water-volume anomalies; cyclone dossiers use storm-track tropical-cyclone heat potential.

graphNodes.name: Peatland Degradation
graphNodes.description: Peatland Degradation is represented here through peatland condition and drained-area change, measured in hectares by condition class, drainage status, land use, and assessment year for mapped peatland complex, basin, country, or reporting region. Peat depth, drainage mapping, land-cover classification, cloud cover, restoration status, and inconsistent national inventories affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Waterborne Pathogen Outbreaks
graphNodes.description: Waterborne Pathogen Outbreaks is represented here through waterborne outbreak signal, measured in epidemiologically linked cases with pathogen and exposure-pathway status for named health jurisdiction or incident area. Case ascertainment, incubation periods, and multiple exposure routes limit attribution.

graphNodes.name: Emergency Response Capacity Exceedance
graphNodes.description: Emergency Response Overload is represented here through austin-Travis County EMS incidents missing the applicable response-time goal, measured in incidents, percent of incidents, and percentage-point shortfall from target for Austin-Travis County EMS system, separated into City of Austin, Travis County outside the city, and priority classes 1 through 5. The public table reports aggregated CAD performance and rounded percentages. Priority coding, dispatch practices, goal definitions, mutual aid, incidents outside the service area, revisions, and incomplete months affect results. A missed response goal can reflect distance, call mix, traffic, dispatch, availability, or other factors and is not proof of capacity exceedance.

graphNodes.name: Zoonotic Disease Outbreaks
graphNodes.description: Zoonotic Disease Outbreaks is represented here through confirmed zoonotic-outbreak incidence and spread, measured in laboratory-confirmed human cases, probable cases, deaths, affected administrative areas, and reproduction or growth estimate by named pathogen and case definition for named outbreak, country, administrative area, exposure setting, and animal-human interface. Under-ascertainment, changing case definitions, diagnostic access, reporting delay, animal surveillance gaps, and uncertain reservoir attribution affect incidence and source estimates.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Erosion
graphNodes.description: Coastal Erosion is represented here through shoreline position change along a declared coastal segment, measured in metres per year for declared habitat, ecosystem, protected area, watershed, coastline, or analysis grid. Survey effort, detectability, taxonomic coverage, map resolution, reference condition, seasonality, and attribution affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Alpine Snowpack Declines
graphNodes.description: Alpine Snowpack Declines is represented here through alpine snow water equivalent and disappearance timing, measured in millimetres snow-water equivalent, snow-covered area, or days to disappearance for named mountain basin, elevation band, or observing grid cell. Gauge sparsity, terrain interpolation, satellite cloud cover, and changing precipitation phase introduce uncertainty.

graphNodes.name: Wetland Drainage
graphNodes.description: Wetland Drainage is represented here through agricultural organic-soil area under drainage, measured in hectares observed under drained use per year for FAOSTAT country, territory, region, or World; cropland and grassland organic soils only. Histosol maps, annual land cover, agricultural-use classification, country boundaries, Tier 1 methods, source flags and revisions affect area estimates.

graphNodes.name: Submarine Cable Landing-Site Concentration and Exposure
graphNodes.description: Submarine Cable Landing-Site Concentration and Exposure is represented here through submarine-cable landing-site concentration and hazard exposure, measured in cables, independent systems, landing stations, geographically diverse routes, shared-risk groups, and exposed capacity reported separately for named country, island, coastline segment, landing station, cable system, or terrestrial backhaul corridor. Public maps omit or generalize routes, ownership and capacity do not equal operational independence, confidential station and backhaul details limit common-mode analysis, and traffic can reroute dynamically.

graphNodes.name: Rice Paddy Methane Emissions
graphNodes.description: Rice Paddy Methane Emissions is represented here through rice-cultivation methane emission, measured in kilograms methane per hectare per crop season for named paddy system or inventory jurisdiction. Methane flux responds to water, organic carbon, soils, temperature, and crop management.

graphNodes.name: Managed-Retreat Decision Pressure
graphNodes.description: Managed Retreat Pressure is represented here through properties or households formally evaluated for managed retreat, measured in properties, households, and percent of exposed stock for declared household population, jurisdiction, market, institution, or disaster-affected area. Reporting coverage, eligibility rules, informal activity, valuation, survey error, attribution, and revisions affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Jet Stream Volatility
graphNodes.description: Jet Stream Volatility is represented here through midlatitude jet latitude, speed, waviness, and persistence anomaly, measured in degrees latitude, meters per second, and days for specified hemisphere, basin, and season. Jet diagnostics depend on definition, reanalysis, season, stratosphere-troposphere coupling, tropical forcing, and internal variability.

graphNodes.name: Glacier Calving Events
graphNodes.description: Glacier Calving Events is represented here through calving-front change and iceberg discharge, measured in meters of front-position change and cubic kilometers or gigatonnes of ice discharge per period for named marine-terminating glacier or ice shelf. Cloud cover, mélange, front delineation, thickness, density, and poorly observed submarine geometry affect event and flux estimates.

graphNodes.name: Wildfire Smoke Hospitalization Burden
graphNodes.description: Wildfire Smoke Hospitalization Burden is represented here through wildfire smoke hospitalization burden, measured in daily cause-specific admissions or attributable rate with case definition for named community, health jurisdiction, or smoke-affected area. Admissions have multiple causes and exposure attribution is uncertain.

graphNodes.name: Cooling Equity Gaps
graphNodes.description: Cooling Equity Gaps is represented here through heat exposure without safe and affordable cooling access, measured in people or households, percentage, and cooling-energy affordability burden within a stated heat threshold and service definition for city, settlement, utility territory, country, or named vulnerable population. Informal housing, unreliable service, indoor conditions, device efficiency, energy prices, income, and population mobility limit comparability.

graphNodes.name: Kelp Forest Collapse
graphNodes.description: Kelp Forest Collapse is represented here through kelp canopy area change, measured in hectares and percent change relative to a fixed seasonal baseline for named kelp forest, coastline segment, sanctuary, or ecoregion. Canopy visibility, species life history, storms, seasonality, water clarity, and survey coverage can mimic or obscure ecological loss.

graphNodes.name: Trophic Cascade Disruption
graphNodes.description: Trophic Cascade Disruption is represented here through trophic interaction and downstream response, measured in abundance, biomass, interaction strength, diet, and downstream vegetation or community response reported separately for named food web, focal taxa, ecosystem, comparison design, and period. Food webs contain compensatory consumers, omnivory, changing diets, and context-dependent interaction strengths.

graphNodes.name: Groundwater Recharge Decline
graphNodes.description: Groundwater Recharge Decline is represented here through groundwater recharge-rate change, measured in millimetres per year or cubic metres per year with aquifer and method stated for named aquifer, recharge zone, catchment, or groundwater model domain. Recharge is commonly modelled rather than directly observed and varies strongly with geology, antecedent moisture, land cover, and climate.

graphNodes.name: Supply Chain Port Bottlenecks
graphNodes.description: Tracks climate-sensitive chokepoints in ports and logistics networks where congestion and disruption spill into wider supply chains.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Property Insurance Nonrenewal
graphNodes.description: Coastal Property Insurance Nonrenewal is represented here through property-insurance nonrenewal rate in declared coastal hazard zones, measured in nonrenewals per 1000 policies for declared household population, jurisdiction, market, institution, or disaster-affected area. Reporting coverage, eligibility rules, informal activity, valuation, survey error, attribution, and revisions affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Cloud Radiative Effect Change
graphNodes.description: Cloud Radiative Effect Change is represented here through satellite cloud radiative-effect change, measured in watts per square meter for shortwave, longwave, and net cloud radiative effect, reported separately with clear-sky definition and uncertainty for CERES footprint, declared grid, cloud regime, ocean basin, or global aggregation. Clear-sky sampling, scene classification, cloud masking, diurnal sampling, instrument calibration, aerosol above clouds, surface albedo, and changing cloud regimes affect estimated trends.

graphNodes.name: Deep-Sea Mining Sediment Plumes
graphNodes.description: Deep-Sea Mining Sediment Plumes is represented here through deep-sea mining sediment plume, measured in suspended sediment concentration, particle-size distribution, plume area or volume, settling flux, and duration for named mining test or operation, discharge depth, water mass, seafloor footprint, and monitoring period. Commercial-scale behavior depends strongly on discharge design, turbulence, thresholds, aggregation, and background nepheloid layers.

graphNodes.name: Pesticide Residues in Surface Water
graphNodes.description: Pesticide Residues in Surface Water is represented here through surface-water pesticide residue concentration and benchmark ratio, measured in micrograms per litre by parent compound or degradate and unitless measured-concentration-to-taxon-specific-benchmark ratio reported separately for named stream, lake, watershed, monitoring station, sampling reach, and upstream use domain. Short runoff pulses are easily missed; reporting limits, degradates, mixtures, flow, season, treatment practices, urban uses, and changing analytical methods affect occurrence and inferred risk.

graphNodes.name: Acid Rain Deposition
graphNodes.description: Acid Rain Deposition is represented here through acidic wet and dry deposition, measured in sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, hydrogen-ion flux, or precipitation chemistry with method for named emitting facility, fleet, corridor, or deposition-monitoring site. Deposition varies with chemistry, weather, and transport.

graphNodes.name: Dryland Degradation
graphNodes.description: Dryland Degradation is represented here through dryland land-degradation extent and condition, measured in hectares and percent of fixed dryland baseline, with land productivity, vegetation cover, soil condition, and carbon-stock components reported separately for named dryland assessment unit, watershed, rangeland, agricultural district, or country reporting boundary. Climate variability, sensor changes, land-cover classification, grazing intensity, crop cycles, soil sampling, choice of baseline, and older global assessment methods can change apparent extent and direction.

graphNodes.name: Atmospheric Ozone-Depleting Substance Burden
graphNodes.description: Atmospheric Ozone-Depleting Substance Burden is represented here through atmospheric ozone-depleting-substance burden, measured in parts per trillion dry-air mole fraction by species and equivalent effective stratospheric chlorine in parts per trillion chlorine-equivalent reported separately for named surface monitoring network and explicitly defined midlatitude or polar stratospheric domain. Species have different lifetimes, transport lags, photolysis fractions, natural contributions, and per-atom ozone-depletion effectiveness; surface abundance and stratospheric reactive loading are not interchangeable.

graphNodes.name: Arctic Amplification
graphNodes.description: Arctic Amplification Rates is represented here through arctic surface-temperature trend relative to the global trend, measured in unitless ratio with degrees Celsius per decade retained for declared station, reanalysis grid, climate region, or global domain. Observational coverage, reanalysis assimilation, model structural spread, baseline choice, and spatial aggregation affect the estimate.

graphNodes.name: Rainforest Savannization
graphNodes.description: Rainforest Savannization is represented here through tropical forest to open-vegetation transition, measured in hectares and percent of fixed forest baseline reclassified with persistence threshold for named tropical-forest biome, ecoregion, or fixed analysis grid. Temporary canopy loss, fire scars, plantations, seasonal phenology, sensor change, and gradual degradation can be confused with a persistent biome transition.

graphNodes.name: Urban Water Rationing
graphNodes.description: Urban Water Rationing is represented here through urban water restriction status, measured in restriction stage, affected connections, and duration for named public-water utility or service area. Policies and restrictions vary by jurisdiction.

graphNodes.name: Asphalt Surface Heat Storage
graphNodes.description: Asphalt Pavement Heat Absorbers is represented here through pavement surface temperature and solar reflectance, measured in degrees Celsius and unitless albedo for named asset, operator service area, network, city, or infrastructure portfolio. Incomplete incident reporting, cascading failures, attribution, asset inventories, customer counts, and overlapping outages affect totals.

graphNodes.name: Heat-Attributable Excess Mortality
graphNodes.description: Heatwave Excess Mortality Rates is represented here through global and WHO-region modelled heat-attributable mortality, measured in deaths and percent of all deaths attributable to heat for declared health surveillance area, city, country, demographic group, or occupational population. Under-ascertainment, coding, exposure misclassification, lag structure, confounding, model choice, and population denominators affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Ambient Air-Quality Standard Exceedance
graphNodes.description: Ambient Air Quality Deficit is represented here through population exposure or days exceeding an applicable ambient air-quality guideline by pollutant, measured in percent population or exceedance days per year, reported separately for declared monitoring site, airshed, waterbody, facility, region, or emissions inventory boundary. Instrument calibration, source apportionment, inventory factors, sampling coverage, chemical transformation, and model resolution affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Population Genetic Bottlenecks
graphNodes.description: Population Genetic Bottlenecks is represented here through population genetic diversity and effective size, measured in heterozygosity, allelic richness, effective population size, inbreeding coefficient, and connectivity estimate by population for named taxon, population units, marker set, sampling design, generation window, and reference period. Marker choice, temporal sampling, population structure, immigration, selection, and small samples alter inferred diversity and effective size.

graphNodes.name: Palm Oil-Driven Forest Clearance
graphNodes.description: Permanent forest conversion associated with expansion of oil-palm plantations, bounded to locations where land-use attribution or supply-area evidence supports the commodity link.

graphNodes.name: Transboundary Fisheries Conflict
graphNodes.description: Transboundary Fisheries Conflict is represented here through international fisheries conflict incidents and severity, measured in events by actor pair, fishery, jurisdiction, incident type, severity, casualties, detention, vessel impact, and duration reported separately for named transboundary stock, fishing ground, exclusive economic zone, high-seas area, bilateral boundary, or regional fisheries body. Public reporting is incomplete and politically uneven; incidents may mix fisheries, territorial, security, labour, piracy, or enforcement motives, while stock and dependence data have different spatial and temporal coverage.

graphNodes.name: Stratospheric Cooling
graphNodes.description: Tracks upper-atmosphere cooling linked to greenhouse forcing and ozone-chemistry interactions.

graphNodes.name: Inland Waterway Fuel Spills
graphNodes.description: Inland Waterway Fuel Spills is represented here through inland-waterway oil discharge, measured in incident count, reported volume, containment status, current velocity, or affected shoreline length for named inland waterway or adjoining shoreline. Reported volumes and downstream fate may be revised after investigation.

graphNodes.name: Coral Reef Fragmentation
graphNodes.description: Coral Reef Fragmentation is represented here through coral-framework fragmentation and structural complexity, measured in fragment count, percent damaged framework, rugosity, or three-dimensional complexity by mapped reef area and survey date for named reef tract, incident perimeter, survey transect, or restoration site. Pre-event baselines, survey visibility, storm attribution, overlapping chronic stress, three-dimensional reconstruction, and detection of buried fragments affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Mountain Pass Avalanches
graphNodes.description: Mountain Pass Avalanches is represented here through avalanche events intersecting a declared mountain transport corridor, measured in events and closure-hours per season for named glacier, ice sheet sector, snow basin, permafrost region, or polar analysis grid. Cloud and surface retrieval, sparse field validation, firn and density assumptions, terrain, sensor transitions, and interpolation affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Dust Storm Frequency
graphNodes.description: Dust Storm Frequency is represented here through sand and dust storm event frequency and exposure, measured in events per season or year, with duration, particulate concentration, aerosol index, visibility, and affected area reported separately for named source region, transport corridor, monitoring network, or receptor population. Cloud screening, surface-monitor coverage, event thresholds, source attribution, transported smoke or pollution, soil moisture, and changing satellite products affect counts and exposure estimates.

graphNodes.name: Ice Shelf Grounding Line Retreat
graphNodes.description: Ice Shelf Grounding Line Retreat is represented here through ice-shelf grounding-line position change, measured in metres per year for named glacier, ice sheet sector, snow basin, permafrost region, or polar analysis grid. Cloud and surface retrieval, sparse field validation, firn and density assumptions, terrain, sensor transitions, and interpolation affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Pollen Allergen Spikes
graphNodes.description: Pollen Allergen Spikes is represented here through airborne allergenic-pollen exposure, measured in grains per cubic metre by taxon and sampling interval, with season start, end, duration, and cumulative count reported separately for named pollen-monitoring station and its stated representativeness area. Different samplers are not always comparable for absolute counts; station coverage, taxon identification, wind transport, rainfall washout, local vegetation, missing observations, and season definitions affect results.

graphNodes.name: Estuary Eutrophication
graphNodes.description: Estuary Eutrophication is represented here through estuary nutrient and eutrophication condition, measured in nitrogen and phosphorus concentration or load, chlorophyll-a, water clarity, dissolved oxygen, affected-system count and hypoxic area or duration reported separately for named estuary, tributary, station network, assessment segment, or worldwide UNEP inventory boundary.
