Sparse sampling, tidal stage, river discharge, nutrient form, internal loading, residence time, stratification, algal composition, sensor drift, and threshold choice affect attribution and area estimates.

graphNodes.name: Migratory Bird Timing, Route, and Stopover Disruption
graphNodes.description: Migratory Bird Timing, Route, and Stopover Disruption is represented here through migratory-bird passage timing, route, and stopover use, measured in birds or radar bioscatter per kilometre per hour, median passage date, days of phenological offset, stopover occupancy or use probability, and habitat area reported separately for named species or guild, radar or observation domain, flyway or route segment, stopover site, breeding and nonbreeding ranges, and annual-cycle boundary. Weather radar cannot always identify species, citizen-science effort changes, routes and cues differ among populations, stopover use varies with weather and habitat, and an earlier date does not by itself indicate harm.

graphNodes.name: Shell Calcification Failures
graphNodes.description: Shell Calcification Failures is represented here through carbonate saturation state and observed shellfish growth or survival impairment, measured in aragonite or calcite saturation state, millimeters, grams, or survival percentage for bounded shellfish habitat, hatchery, or estuary. Responses vary strongly by species, life stage, acclimation, co-stressors, and local water chemistry.

graphNodes.name: Arctic Pack Ice Drift
graphNodes.description: Arctic Pack Ice Drift is represented here through arctic sea-ice drift speed and direction, measured in kilometres per day and degrees bearing for named glacier, ice sheet sector, snow basin, permafrost region, or polar analysis grid. Cloud and surface retrieval, sparse field validation, firn and density assumptions, terrain, sensor transitions, and interpolation affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Amphibian Chytrid Infection Prevalence and Mortality
graphNodes.description: Amphibian Chytrid Infection Prevalence and Mortality is represented here through amphibian chytrid infection prevalence, intensity, and mortality, measured in percent polymerase-chain-reaction-positive individuals, genomic equivalents per skin swab, diagnosed deaths, apparent survival, and occupied breeding sites reported separately for named pathogen species, amphibian host taxon and life stage, wetland or stream site, population, sampling region, and surveillance boundary. Detection varies with swabbing, season, temperature, host species, life stage, infection load, prior exposure, and imperfect detection; infection can be widespread and subclinical without attributable mortality.

graphNodes.name: Early-Warning Coverage Gap
graphNodes.description: Early Warning Coverage Gaps is represented here through country reporting gap for the existence of multi-hazard early-warning systems under Sendai Target G, measured in percentage of countries, derived complement for declared household population, jurisdiction, market, institution, or disaster-affected area. Reporting coverage, eligibility rules, informal activity, valuation, survey error, attribution, and revisions affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Black Carbon Deposition
graphNodes.description: Black Carbon Deposition is represented here through black-carbon deposition in snow or ice and surface-albedo anomaly, measured in nanograms per gram and dimensionless albedo for bounded snow, glacier, or sea-ice surface. Deposition is highly heterogeneous and darkening also depends on dust, snow age, meltwater scavenging, and sensor retrieval.

graphNodes.name: Glacial Siltation Streams
graphNodes.description: Glacial Siltation Streams is represented here through glacier-fed stream suspended-sediment concentration and flux, measured in milligrams per liter and tonnes per day or season with discharge, grain-size, and sampling method stated for named proglacial stream, gauging station, downstream lake, reservoir, or fjord. Short-lived peaks, sparse winter data, rating-curve hysteresis, bedload, changing glacier drainage, grain size, and station placement affect annual loads.

graphNodes.name: Jellyfish Bloom Frequency and Biomass
graphNodes.description: Jellyfish Bloom Frequency and Biomass is represented here through jellyfish bloom frequency, biomass, and duration, measured in individuals per cubic metre, biomass, occupied area, event duration, and recurrence by taxon and method for named coastal water body, taxon, life stage, depth, survey platform, season, and baseline. Patchiness, life-cycle stage, currents, observation effort, taxonomic ambiguity, and episodic recruitment complicate trend inference.

graphNodes.name: Cryoconite Hole Expansion
graphNodes.description: Cryoconite Hole Expansion is represented here through cryoconite-hole surface area and depth under a declared survey protocol, measured in square metres and centimetres for named glacier, ice sheet sector, snow basin, permafrost region, or polar analysis grid. Cloud and surface retrieval, sparse field validation, firn and density assumptions, terrain, sensor transitions, and interpolation affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Bark Beetle Epidemics
graphNodes.description: Bark Beetle Epidemics is represented here through bark-beetle outbreak extent and tree mortality, measured in hectares affected and trees killed per hectare by named beetle and host species, survey method, and damage year for named forest stand, aerial-detection survey polygon, management unit, ecoregion, or species range. Aerial surveys can miss low-severity damage, attribution becomes harder after needle loss, multiple mortality agents co-occur, and survey coverage and thresholds vary.

graphNodes.name: Old-Growth Forest Logging
graphNodes.description: Old-Growth Forest Logging is represented here through old-growth forest harvest area, measured in hectares harvested by method and reporting period for named forest management unit using an explicit old-growth definition. Old-growth definitions vary by forest type and jurisdiction, while selective harvest and collateral damage can be underdetected remotely.

graphNodes.name: Savanna Tree-Cover Decline
graphNodes.description: Savanna Tree-Cover Decline is represented here through savanna woody-canopy cover change, measured in percent woody cover, hectares, stem density, basal area, and persistence relative to a fixed baseline for named savanna ecosystem, fixed plot or grid, land-use and fire-history boundary, and period. Rainfall variability, fire exclusion, grazing, browsing, woody encroachment, clearing, and sensor definitions can produce opposite trends.

graphNodes.name: Particulate Soot Levels
graphNodes.description: Tracks soot and black-carbon particle burden as both an air-quality hazard and a climate-relevant aerosol load.

graphNodes.name: Pesticide Spray Drift
graphNodes.description: Pesticide Spray Drift is represented here through off-target pesticide drift exposure, measured in active-ingredient mass or concentration by air, deposition, surface, or biological sample with distance, duration, and application context stated for named application field, intended treatment boundary, downwind receptor, habitat, or water body. Wind shifts, inversions, volatilization, equipment, droplet size, sampling timing, degradation, background use, and incomplete application records affect exposure estimates.

graphNodes.name: Estuarine Nursery Loss
graphNodes.description: Tracks degradation of estuarine juvenile habitat under hypoxia, warming, and pollution stress that weakens fishery recruitment.

graphNodes.name: Ice Algae Pigmentation
graphNodes.description: Ice Algae Pigmentation is represented here through snow or ice algal pigment biomass and coincident surface albedo, measured in micrograms chlorophyll per square metre and unitless albedo for named glacier, ice sheet sector, snow basin, permafrost region, or polar analysis grid. Cloud and surface retrieval, sparse field validation, firn and density assumptions, terrain, sensor transitions, and interpolation affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Mineral Dust Deposition on Snow
graphNodes.description: Mineral Dust Deposition on Snow is represented here through mineral-dust mass loading and snow albedo, measured in grams per square metre mineral-dust loading, unitless spectral or broadband albedo, and watts per square metre absorbed shortwave energy reported separately for named snow basin, sampling transect, satellite pixel, mountain range, or watershed with source-region context. Dust can be buried and re-emerge during melt; snow grain growth, black carbon, algae, forest litter, clouds, slope, aspect, sensor resolution, and mixed pixels also change reflectance and energy absorption.

graphNodes.name: Heavy-Metal Bioaccumulation
graphNodes.description: Heavy-Metal Bioaccumulation is represented here through metal concentration in environment and biota, measured in compound- or species-specific concentration in water, sediment, food, and tissue with wet or dry basis stated for named site, metal species, organism, tissue, life stage, food web, sampling period, and reference site. Essentiality, speciation, bioavailability, metabolism, growth dilution, diet, season, and trophic structure differ strongly among metals and taxa.

graphNodes.name: Glacier Hydrologic System Floods
graphNodes.description: Glacier Hydrologic System Floods is represented here through glacier-related outburst flood peak discharge and volume, measured in cubic metres per second and million cubic metres for declared basin, aquifer, utility, catchment, floodplain, or administrative reporting area. Gauge and well coverage, withdrawals, return flows, groundwater-surface-water exchange, infrastructure reporting, model resolution, and revisions affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Wetland Peat Fires
graphNodes.description: Wetland Peat Fires is represented here through peat-fire burned area and carbon emission, measured in hectares burned and tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent with peat depth, combustion factor, and reporting interval stated for mapped peatland fire perimeter, province, basin, or country. Subsurface smouldering, burn depth, peat bulk density, emission factors, obscured satellite detections, and repeated burning drive large uncertainty.

graphNodes.name: Convective Available Potential Energy and Inhibition Anomaly
graphNodes.description: Convective Available Potential Energy and Inhibition Anomaly is represented here through convective available potential energy and inhibition anomaly, measured in joules per kilogram for parcel-specific CAPE and CIN, with lifted index, humidity, shear, and vertical motion reported separately for named sounding station, satellite pixel, reanalysis grid, forecast domain, or climatological region. Values vary sharply with parcel choice, moisture and surface observations; satellite and reanalysis retrievals smooth vertical structure, and unentraining parcel theory overstates realized updraft energy.

graphNodes.name: Ice Cap Decapitation
graphNodes.description: Ice Cap Decapitation is represented here through ice-cap summit area and mass change, measured in square kilometres and gigatonnes per year for named glacier, ice sheet sector, snow basin, permafrost region, or polar analysis grid. Cloud and surface retrieval, sparse field validation, firn and density assumptions, terrain, sensor transitions, and interpolation affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Riparian Bank Erosion
graphNodes.description: Riparian Bank Erosion is represented here through riparian bank erosion and retreat, measured in metres per year, eroded area or volume, sediment mass, and bank-failure events with reach method stated for named river reach, bank side, floodplain, vegetation zone, flow record, and survey period. Bank retreat is episodic and varies with substrate, vegetation, channel geometry, floods, dams, grazing, and measurement interval.

graphNodes.name: Nighttime Heat Retention
graphNodes.description: Nighttime Heat Retention is represented here through nighttime urban-rural air-temperature difference, measured in degrees Celsius with urban and reference sites, height, local time, and averaging window stated for named city and matched rural or intra-urban reference network. Station siting, urban morphology, wind, cloud cover, humidity, advection, season, and the rural reference affect the measured difference.

graphNodes.name: Nunatak Habitat Shrinkage
graphNodes.description: Nunatak Habitat Shrinkage is represented here through ice-free nunatak habitat area and connectivity, measured in hectares and nearest-neighbour distance for declared habitat, ecosystem, protected area, watershed, coastline, or analysis grid. Survey effort, detectability, taxonomic coverage, map resolution, reference condition, seasonality, and attribution affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Functional Habitat Connectivity Loss
graphNodes.description: Functional Habitat Connectivity Loss is represented here through global terrestrial habitat structural-connectivity gap, measured in percent of forest and protected-area network for global forest and terrestrial protected-area network. Structural connectivity is not species-specific functional connectivity; map resolution, patch thresholds and protected-area boundaries affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Pacific Walker Circulation Variability
graphNodes.description: Pacific Walker Circulation Variability is represented here through pacific Walker circulation strength and longitude, measured in standardized index or pascals sea-level-pressure gradient, metres per second zonal wind, pascals per second vertical velocity, and degrees longitude reported separately for equatorial Pacific with explicitly stated western and eastern boxes, pressure levels, reanalysis or station network. Different indices, sparse early observations, reanalysis changes, ENSO, volcanic forcing, tropical-basin interactions, and internal decadal variability can change the inferred magnitude or sign of a trend.

graphNodes.name: Fjord Sedimentation Pulses
graphNodes.description: Fjord Sedimentation Pulses is represented here through fjord sedimentation pulse, measured in site-specific discharge, suspended-sediment concentration, sediment flux, deposit thickness, or gravity-flow count for named glacier-fed fjord. Flux depends on storage, calving, routing, and basin geometry.

graphNodes.name: Transformer Heat Failure Risk
graphNodes.description: Transformer Heat Failure Risk is represented here through transformer thermal failure risk, measured in winding hot-spot temperature in degrees Celsius with percent rated load, ambient temperature, asset age, and insulation condition for named distribution or power transformer and its served circuit or substation. Sensor placement, unobserved winding hot spots, cooling performance, moisture, prior insulation damage, load harmonics, and asset-specific design affect inferred risk.

graphNodes.name: Freeze-Thaw Rock Fracturing
graphNodes.description: Freeze-Thaw Rock Fracturing is represented here through freeze–thaw fracture displacement, measured in site-specific temperature, cycle count, water pressure, fracture aperture, joint geometry, or displacement for named rock slope or cliff. Rockfall has multiple triggers and local rock-mass properties dominate.

graphNodes.name: Overstory Tree Mortality
graphNodes.description: Overstory Tree Mortality is represented here through overstory tree mortality rate and area, measured in annual mortality rate, dead stems per hectare, basal-area mortality, canopy area, and cause attribution by species for named forest type, plot or mapped area, overstory definition, species, disturbance history, and period. Mortality attribution is confounded by interacting drought, heat, insects, disease, fire, competition, and delayed death.

graphNodes.name: Airborne Microplastic Concentration and Deposition
graphNodes.description: Airborne Microplastic Concentration and Deposition is represented here through airborne microplastic concentration and deposition flux, measured in polymer-confirmed particles per cubic metre of air and particles per square metre per day of wet or dry deposition reported separately, stratified by size, morphology, and polymer for named indoor or outdoor sampling site, airshed, deposition station, source facility, trajectory domain, and land or water receptor. Fibres and fragments occur in heterogeneous particle mixtures; contamination, visual misidentification, sampler design, lower size limit, polymer-confirmation coverage, recovery, and the lack of standardized methods can dominate comparisons.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Saltwater Intrusion
graphNodes.description: Coastal Saltwater Intrusion is represented here through coastal freshwater-saltwater interface, measured in pumping volume, hydraulic head, salinity concentration, water level, or interface position for named coastal aquifer or well field. Intrusion modes and salinity sources vary strongly by hydrogeologic setting.

graphNodes.name: Tundra Shrub Expansion
graphNodes.description: Tundra Shrub Expansion is represented here through tundra shrub cover, height, or biomass, measured in site-specific temperature, day count, moisture, thaw depth, shrub cover, height, or biomass for named Arctic tundra landscape. Greening and shrub expansion vary by taxon, region, and disturbance history.

graphNodes.name: North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre Circulation Strength
graphNodes.description: North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre Circulation Strength is represented here through north Atlantic subpolar-gyre circulation strength, measured in square metres per second squared of wind-stress curl, centimetres of sea-surface-height anomaly or gradient, metres per second of geostrophic velocity, and Sverdrups of named boundary or gyre transport reported separately for declared Labrador, Irminger, Iceland, Rockall, eastern or full North Atlantic subpolar-gyre domain with contour, depth, section, and basin boundary stated. No single universal index exists; altimetric height includes steric and mass effects, horizontal circulation differs from overturning, wind and buoyancy forcing can oppose each other, and regional sectors respond differently.

graphNodes.name: Shelf-Sea Hypoxia
graphNodes.description: Shelf-Sea Hypoxia is represented here through continental-shelf bottom-water hypoxia, measured in milligrams per liter or milliliters per liter dissolved oxygen with hypoxic area, water-column thickness, duration, depth, threshold and global site inventory reported separately for named continental-shelf survey grid, transect, bottom-water station network, model domain, or declared global assessment boundary. Sparse transects, sensor drift, short-lived mixing, tidal and upwelling variability, threshold choice, and interpolation across unobserved shelf water affect area and duration estimates.

graphNodes.name: Freshwater Mussel Population Decline
graphNodes.description: Freshwater Mussel Population Decline is represented here through freshwater mussel population and recruitment, measured in density, catch per unit effort, occupancy, species richness, survival, recruitment, and size structure by survey method for named river reach, mussel taxon and host context, habitat, survey design, and assessment period. Imperfect detection, patchy beds, long life spans, episodic recruitment, host dynamics, flow, pollution, and unexplained mass mortality affect trends.

graphNodes.name: Lightning Flash Density and Seasonality Anomaly
graphNodes.description: Lightning Flash Density and Seasonality Anomaly is represented here through lightning flash density, extent, and seasonality anomaly, measured in flashes per square kilometre per time interval, flash extent area, radiant energy, and season timing reported separately for named GLM field of view, LIS or OTD sampling domain, ground-network domain, fixed grid, or climate region. Satellite and ground networks observe different discharge components; detection efficiency, orbital or viewing geometry, clustering algorithms, network upgrades, day-night background, and short records can create apparent changes.

graphNodes.name: Coral Larval Survival and Recruitment Failure
graphNodes.description: Coral Larval Survival and Recruitment Failure is represented here through coral larval survival, settlement, and recruitment, measured in survival percentage, settlement percentage, or recruits per square meter by species and cohort for named reef, nursery, settlement array, or experimental population. Spawning variability, dispersal, predation, settlement substrate, parental effects, heat, chemistry, disease, and sampling timing affect survival and recruitment.

graphNodes.name: River Network Fragmentation
graphNodes.description: Riverine Habitat Fragmentation is represented here through global long-river network fragmentation, measured in percent of rivers longer than 1,000 kilometres and connected river kilometres for global river network. Connectivity is taxon-, life-stage-, flow- and scale-specific; the long-river statistic does not describe every stream.

graphNodes.name: Mountain Forest Cover and Treeline Contraction
graphNodes.description: Mountain Forest Cover and Treeline Contraction is represented here through mountain-forest cover and treeline contraction, measured in hectares and percent cover change, metres elevation or kilometres latitude of boundary movement, and tree density or basal area reported separately for named mountain range, elevation band, forest type, species assemblage, ecotone, fixed land-cover grid, and disturbance perimeter. Upper boundaries may expand while dry lower margins contract; fire, insects, harvest, classification change, delayed regeneration, and transient canopy loss can mimic a persistent climate-driven range change.

graphNodes.name: Atmospheric River Intensification
graphNodes.description: Atmospheric River Intensification is represented here through atmospheric-river integrated vapor transport intensity and duration, measured in kilograms per metre per second peak integrated vapor transport, hours duration, and event category with detection algorithm stated for named coastal transect, watershed, landfall corridor, or atmospheric-river catalog domain. Catalogs differ by threshold, geometry, reanalysis, resolution, landfall definition, and duration; topography and antecedent conditions strongly change precipitation and runoff impacts.

graphNodes.name: Equatorial Pacific Trade-Wind Anomaly
graphNodes.description: Signed departure of equatorial Pacific easterly trade winds from their seasonal baseline. Weaker or reversed easterlies support El Niño development; stronger easterlies support La Niña development.

graphNodes.name: Blue Carbon Habitat Loss
graphNodes.description: Blue Carbon Habitat Loss is represented here through coastal blue-carbon habitat area and carbon-stock loss, measured in hectares lost and tonnes carbon or carbon dioxide equivalent released or sequestration capacity lost for global assessment or named salt-marsh, mangrove, or seagrass assessment area. Below-ground stocks, erosion fate, remineralization, mapping resolution, and counterfactual sequestration vary by habitat and method.

graphNodes.name: Atmospheric Hydroxyl Sink Weakening
graphNodes.description: Atmospheric Hydroxyl Sink Weakening is represented here through tropospheric hydroxyl oxidation capacity and methane lifetime, measured in molecules per cubic centimetre or normalized hydroxyl-radical anomaly, years chemical lifetime, and teragrams per year chemical sink reported separately for global troposphere or named chemistry-model and observational-inversion domain. The radical is too short-lived for a dense direct global network; inversions and models disagree on trends and are sensitive to emissions, transport, chemistry, observational constraints, and spatial weighting.

graphNodes.name: Stratospheric Ozone Column Depletion and Recovery
graphNodes.description: Stratospheric Ozone Column Depletion and Recovery is represented here through stratospheric ozone-column depletion and recovery, measured in Dobson Units and million square kilometres below the 220-DU Antarctic threshold for Southern Hemisphere Antarctic ozone-hole domain south of 40 degrees south, with the seasonal averaging window stated. Polar-vortex dynamics, temperature, aerosols, sunlight, transport, sensor transitions, missing-orbit assimilation and the selected seasonal window affect annual ozone-hole area and minimum column ozone.

graphNodes.name: Aviation Condensation Trails
graphNodes.description: Aviation Condensation Trails is represented here through persistent contrail and aviation-induced cloudiness burden, measured in kilometres of detected trail, square kilometres or percent cloud fraction, hours persistence, optical depth, and watts per square metre forcing reported separately for named flight-information region, air corridor, satellite scene, or model domain. Natural cirrus, cloud overlap, ice-supersaturation forecasts, satellite detection, attribution to individual flights, optical properties, day-night balance, and model efficacy dominate uncertainty.

graphNodes.name: Compound Coastal Flooding
graphNodes.description: Compound Coastal Flooding is represented here through co-occurring coastal water-level and runoff or precipitation flood events, measured in events and inundated square kilometres per year for declared basin, aquifer, utility, catchment, floodplain, or administrative reporting area. Gauge and well coverage, withdrawals, return flows, groundwater-surface-water exchange, infrastructure reporting, model resolution, and revisions affect estimates.

graphNodes.name: Fisheries Range Redistribution
graphNodes.description: Fisheries Range Redistribution is represented here through marine-stock distribution centroid and boundary change, measured in kilometres and degrees latitude or metres depth per decade, with occupancy, biomass weighting, survey domain, and uncertainty stated for named stock, species, survey programme, shelf, management area, or transboundary marine region. Survey coverage, gear catchability, seasonal movement, age structure, stock definition, population abundance, habitat, prey, fishing pressure, ocean variability, and model choice affect apparent shifts.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Aquifer Salinization
graphNodes.description: Tracks degradation of coastal groundwater quality where salinization and overdraw reduce the usability of local aquifer supplies.

graphNodes.name: Food Insecurity
graphNodes.description: Uncertain or constrained physical and economic access to sufficient, safe, nutritious food.

graphNodes.name: Nutrient Pollution
graphNodes.description: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus loading that degrades fresh and coastal waters.

graphNodes.name: Seagrass Meadow Decline
graphNodes.description: Persistent loss or degradation of mapped seagrass habitat and its ecological functions.

graphNodes.name: Urban Heat Island
graphNodes.description: Urban areas remaining warmer than a bounded non-urban reference because of land cover, morphology, and anthropogenic heat.

graphNodes.name: Dam and Diversion Infrastructure
graphNodes.description: Dams, weirs, and water-diversion structures that can interrupt river connectivity, alter flow, and change habitat conditions within a bounded river network.

graphNodes.name: Road-Stream Crossing Barriers
graphNodes.description: Culverts, fords, bridges, and tide gates whose geometry or flow conditions impede aquatic-organism movement in a bounded stream network.

graphNodes.name: Levee and Channelization Works
graphNodes.description: Engineered levees, channel straightening, and floodplain disconnection that can reduce lateral river-floodplain connectivity and habitat complexity.

graphNodes.name: Humanitarian Response Funding Shortfall
graphNodes.description: Appeals that remain unfunded force reduction, delay, or termination of life-saving response activities.

graphNodes.name: Humanitarian Access Constraints
graphNodes.description: Conflict, bureaucratic restrictions, and attacks on personnel can prevent aid from reaching crisis-affected communities.

graphNodes.name: Humanitarian Surge Demand
graphNodes.description: Concurrent disasters, displacement, and conflict can raise the number of people requiring time-sensitive assistance faster than response capacity expands.

graphNodes.name: Agricultural Groundwater Withdrawal
graphNodes.description: Groundwater withdrawn for irrigation in a named aquifer and reporting period; it is not a proxy for all agriculture.

graphNodes.name: Municipal Groundwater Withdrawal
graphNodes.description: Public-supply groundwater withdrawal within a named aquifer and reporting period; it is not a proxy for all urban water demand.

graphNodes.name: Industrial Groundwater Withdrawal
graphNodes.description: Industrial, mining, thermoelectric, or other reported non-agricultural groundwater withdrawal within a named aquifer and reporting period.

graphNodes.name: Agricultural Nitrogen Application
graphNodes.description: Synthetic or organic nitrogen applied to managed soils within a named crop, area, and reporting period.

graphNodes.name: Anaerobic Manure Lagoon Operation
graphNodes.description: Operation of a named manure lagoon, bounded by animal type, manure loading, retention time, temperature, treatment state, and reporting period.

graphNodes.name: Cattle Stocking Density
graphNodes.description: Documented cattle liveweight or animal units per paddock area and grazing interval.

graphNodes.name: Coal-Power Sulfur Emissions
graphNodes.description: Measured sulfur-dioxide emissions from named coal-fired electricity generating units.

graphNodes.name: Agricultural Soil Compaction
graphNodes.description: Measured compaction or root-restricting condition in a named agricultural soil profile.

graphNodes.name: Urban Hydrologic Supply Shortfall
graphNodes.description: Measured shortfall in a utility’s surface-water, reservoir, or groundwater supply relative to demand and operating rules.

graphNodes.name: Urban Water-Demand Peak
graphNodes.description: Measured peak demand above a named utility’s available supply or treatment capacity.

graphNodes.name: Urban Distribution Water Loss
graphNodes.description: Documented physical or apparent loss in a named public-water distribution system.

graphNodes.name: Urban Source-Water Treatment Constraint
graphNodes.description: Documented raw-water quality or treatment constraint reducing a named utility’s usable supply.

graphNodes.name: Wildfire Smoke PM2.5 Exposure
graphNodes.description: Population-weighted wildfire-specific fine-particle exposure for a named place and time window.

graphNodes.name: Wildfire Smoke Exposure Duration
graphNodes.description: Duration and recurrence of a documented smoke event above a stated exposure threshold.

graphNodes.name: Surface-Water Inflow Deficit
graphNodes.description: Documented precipitation, streamflow, or runoff deficit to a named surface-water body.

graphNodes.name: Surface-Water Evaporative Loss
graphNodes.description: Measured or modeled evaporative loss from a named lake, wetland, or river reach.

graphNodes.name: Surface-Water Groundwater-Exchange Shift
graphNodes.description: Documented change in groundwater inflow to, or seepage from, a named surface-water body.

graphNodes.name: Surface-Water Withdrawal Pressure
graphNodes.description: Documented diversion or withdrawal relative to inflow and storage for a named surface-water body.

graphNodes.name: Coastal Groundwater Withdrawal
graphNodes.description: Reported freshwater pumping from a named coastal aquifer or well field.

graphNodes.name: Coal Power CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated coal power co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Gas Power CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated gas power co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Oil-Fired Power CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated oil-fired power co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Coal Industrial-Heat CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated coal industrial-heat co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Gas Industrial-Heat CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated gas industrial-heat co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Cement-Kiln Fuel CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated cement-kiln fuel co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Metal Industry Fossil CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated metal industry fossil co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Chemical Industry Fossil CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated chemical industry fossil co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Petroleum Refining and Other Energy Industries Fossil CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated petroleum refining and other energy industries fossil co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Civil Aviation Fossil CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated civil aviation fossil co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Water-Borne Navigation Fossil CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated water-borne navigation fossil co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Passenger Road-Fuel CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated passenger road-fuel co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Diesel Freight CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated diesel freight co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Railway Fossil CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated railway fossil co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Residential Gas-Heating CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated residential gas-heating co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Commercial Gas-Heating CO2 Output
graphNodes.description: Measured or inventory-estimated commercial gas-heating co2 output within a named reporting geography and period.

graphNodes.name: Oil Building-Heat CO2 Output
